s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and adnexal mass with chronic unilateral lower limb edema
salient_findings: Non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
Firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant
key_facts: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg
Regular menses
No tobacco or alcohol use
Afebrile, blood pressure 110/80 mmHg, pulse 88 beats/min
Respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Cardiac and respiratory examinations were unremarkable
Neurologic exam was normal
Abdomen revealed a firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm
Bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
Normal baseline hematologic, biochemical, thyroid, renal, and HIV/HBV/HCV serologies
Tumor markers within reference range
Pap smear was negative
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Concerning imaging findings for an ovarian neoplasm and presence of a large adnexal mass

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and imaging characteristics to ovarian cystadenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common type of ovarian cancer and possible cause of adnexal mass and abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Ovarian teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of adnexal mass and can present with abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Less common type of ovarian cancer, but still a possible cause of adnexal mass and abdominal pain

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large abdominal mass, confirmed by imaging to be a solid-cystic lesion in the right adnexa, along with the concern for an ovarian neoplasm based on imaging findings despite normal tumor markers, points towards a diagnosis of ovarian cystadenocarcinoma. This diagnosis best explains the key facts without contradiction, considering the patient's age, symptoms, and imaging results.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the information provided does not specifically suggest mucinous characteristics.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to mucinous, the specifics pointing directly to serous type are not provided in the vignette.

rejected.label: Ovarian teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas are a type of germ cell tumor and can present with a wide range of symptoms, but the imaging description and concern for malignancy make cystadenocarcinoma more likely.

rejected.label: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Clear cell carcinoma is less common and typically has a distinct histological appearance; the vignette does not provide specific evidence pointing towards this diagnosis.
